Rain outlook for IIT Tirupati campus

Nested WRF model run (9 km, 3 km and 1 km grids) by the HYDROS Lab, started from GFS data of 25 Oct 2026 12:00 UTC (17:30 IST). Shown as the chance of rain in 3-hour blocks, in Indian Standard Time. This run covers 25 Oct 17:30 to 27 Oct 17:30 IST.

Please read: this is a research product, not an official forecast. The model is more useful for saying when rain may come than how much, so no rainfall amounts are shown. The chances below are model-based, not calibrated probabilities. For warnings use IMD (mausam.imd.gov.in).

How to read this · limits
  • What the chance means. Each of the three model grids (9, 3 and 1 km) is checked for the share of its cells within 25 km of the campus that show rain (1 mm or more in the 3 hours; heavier rain means 7.5 mm or more). The three shares are averaged and rounded to the nearest 10 %. Levels: low under 25 %, medium 25–50 %, high 50–75 %, very high above 75 %.
  • Not a calibrated probability. The three grids come from the same starting data, so they are not independent opinions. Agreement between them is a good sign, not a guarantee. This run has not yet been checked against campus reports and IMD for the coming days.
  • Track record so far (2–3 events): the 3 km grid caught when rain started and stopped on 21 Oct and on the night of 22–23 Oct, but it also gave rain on drizzle-only days and over-estimated the amount on 22 Oct. The 9 km grid was erratic in amount (too low on 21 Oct, several times too high on 17 Oct). The 1 km grid was closest on the drizzle day but placed some rain about 10 km away. This is why amounts are not shown.
  • Last forecast check. For the night of 23–24 Oct the previous run (GFS of 23 Oct 12 UTC) was dry, as observed. For 24–25 Oct, compared with IMD gridded rainfall for the campus cell (5.6 mm for that day), its 9 km and 3 km grids were roughly three to four times too wet and the 1 km grid was close. The run before that (GFS of 22 Oct 00 UTC) was 12 to 19 times too wet for the same day. So the newest start has done better, but this is only one day of checking.
  • The forecast is one model run from one set of starting data, and it gets less reliable the further ahead you look.
  • Coastline is approximate. Map covers 7–19°N, 73–85°E (Arabian Sea, Laccadive Sea and Bay of Bengal): the 9 km grid everywhere, with the finer 3 km grid inside the thin box around the campus.
